Drawability: Pages are drawn by an image model, one page per generation, from each character's and location's sheet, and a page drifts when it carries too much. So: at most 4 panels a page; at most 3 named characters in one panel; one location a page where the story allows (every new location needs its own sheet); no crowd that must be recognisable; a big moment gets a splash (one panel, the whole page). Count pages this way, not by comic convention. Every page you make keeps to it.

# Key pages - locked by the showrunner

These pages are finished. Their look is the look of the whole book. Their words - every caption and line below - are used exactly as written, on that page, and never edited. Their layout is that page's layout.

## What the key pages do not lock

The key pages are chapter 3 as drawn: they set the book's style, their own words and their own
panels. They do not override the canon. Where a page draws something differently from
characters.md or rules/, the canon wins.

- **Bi11bot is off-model in these pages.** He is drawn with a teal-blue metal body and no scarf.
  Take the style and his small size, not his design: he is child-sized, built from aged brass,
  titanium and ceramic ivory, with two expressive optical eyes in soft blue and amber, an old
  rust-red scarf, foldable to fit in a backpack, and never menacing (characters.md; rules/characters.md).
